sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Project settings in one file
sections.what: Holds all project settings in one place: identity, Python version, build tool, test runner, formatter and import sorter.
sections.why: Likely reason: one file keeps the tool settings together.
sections.watch_out: The placeholder web addresses point to a made-up repository, so the links are wrong until they are replaced.

summary: Holds the project's settings: name, version, license, minimum Python version, build tool, and the settings for the test runner, formatter and import sorter.
purpose: Tells the build, test and formatting tools how to handle this backend.
why: Likely reason: a standard single settings file for a Python project.
how: 1. Names the project and its version, and requires Python 3.10 or newer. 2. Gives web links and an author name. 3. Sets setuptools as the build tool. 4. Tells pytest to look in the tests folder and always create a coverage report. 5. Sets black and isort to a line length of 100.
inputs: Read by pip, setuptools, pytest, black and isort when they run.
outputs: No direct output. It changes how those tools behave. Running tests creates a coverage report folder.
risks: The web links point to a placeholder account (yourusername). The file refers to README.md, which must exist for packaging. Each test run writes a coverage report to disk.
debug: If installation fails, check the README reference and the Python version. If tests create an unexpected report folder, that comes from the addopts line. If no tests are found, check the tests folder name and the file name pattern.
